newFindings.title: Rolling upgrade falsely advertises a compatible computer
newFindings.trigger: Current supervisor/connector reuse a real prefeature session host while a harmless native job is still running.
newFindings.observed: Connector advertises wire protocol5, but retained host lacks chat.request and replies -32001. New recovery barrier blocks file access, terminal kill and the running job’s proc.kill. Host maintenance waits for idle while normal stop controls are blocked.
newFindings.cause: Host contract stays1 across incompatible dispatch changes. Connector advertises its own protocol and release instead of proving the host can serve those methods. Host reuse/maintenance compares release version without build identity.
newFindings.fix: Negotiate/version host chat capability before connector handover. Never advertise unsupported protocol. Coordinate required maintenance and retain safe stop controls without bypassing ownership/deletion fences.

newFindings.title: Imported native history does not acquire its own attachment pins
newFindings.trigger: Real Codex driver imports saved attachment references into a sibling conversation. Expire or delete the source chat.
newFindings.observed: Retained imported message still references the file, but source pin removal lets GC erase its sealed blob. Attachment becomes unreadable. Reproduced for both retention and source-tab deletion, with zero turn/start calls.
newFindings.cause: Native history enrichment reads task-wide saved content without creating a durable destination-owned attachment reference. Retention counts references only inside the source store owning the pin.
newFindings.fix: Acquire verified destination pins atomically with imported/forked history before exposing it. Blob lifetime must follow every retained reference, not only the first conversation that stored a pin.
newFindings.test: content-third-pass.test.ts — native import pins attachment (retention / deletion)

newFindings.title: Deleted chat text remains in the host notification journal
newFindings.trigger: Real session host buffers a normalized user-message while event delivery is unacknowledged. Permanently delete task and restart host.
newFindings.observed: Computer tombstone survives and SQLite events count is zero. hooks-*.json still contains full deleted message text. Successful event acknowledgement drains the journal in the control.
newFindings.cause: SessionTransport journals every event, including full chat-runtime payloads, outside the per-hub chat database. Chat deletion has no cleanup path for this copy.
newFindings.fix: Use durable storage/outbox replay for chat content and persist only necessary retry metadata. Safely migrate or erase existing journal copies by owner during deletion/retention; preserve unrelated native hook delivery.
newFindings.test: journal-third-pass.test.ts — task deletion and host restart erase buffered notifications

newFindings.title: Retention breaks full session counts and first-prompt labels
newFindings.trigger: Codex session handshake anchor is old, but 601 user messages are still recent and retained.
newFindings.observed: After expiry, Sessions summary falls from601 to500 and first prompt becomes question101. The retained601 messages themselves remain present.
newFindings.cause: Retention removes turn-init/session anchor. Summary reconstruction cannot attribute remaining events and falls back to bounded500-item prompt recall.
newFindings.fix: Preserve compact session/range identity when expiring content anchors. Compute summaries from retained events without relying on composer recall limits.
newFindings.test: content-third-pass.test.ts — retained messages keep full summaries

newFindings.title: Read-only archive/export omits unsent queued text
newFindings.trigger: Create a valid backup containing an unsent message and attachment, delete live task, restore archive, read through supported archive API.
newFindings.observed: Snapshot has queue row, but archive.records whitelist omits it. UI JSON export uses that API and cannot expose unsent text or its attachment. Live queue behavior is unaffected.
newFindings.cause: Archive record projection includes draft/prompt/workspace/thread/diagnostics but excludes queue; export extracts attachments only from events and drafts.
newFindings.fix: Expose queued user content in read-only recovery/export without replaying operations or claiming provider resumability. Include its sealed attachments.
newFindings.test: content-third-pass.test.ts — read-only archive exposes unsent queue text

newFindings.title: A deleted child stays in the parent thread list
newFindings.trigger: Migrate parent and child, delete child via actual tab trigger, deliver lifecycle deletion and ACK, reopen runtime.
newFindings.observed: Parent still lists deleted child and its original title. Selecting the stale entry cannot open the tombstoned child. This is a dead-entry correctness issue, not a separate privacy-erasure claim.
newFindings.cause: Child tombstone clears child content but leaves parent’s thread record; listForParent returns records without checking child liveness.
newFindings.fix: Reconcile parent thread references and notify parent after child deletion. Keep deletion fences durable and preserve valid parent history.
newFindings.test: content-third-pass.test.ts — acknowledged child deletion removes live-list entry

newFindings.title: Search can hide a real hub match behind a placeholder
newFindings.trigger: Newer redacted PC locator and older real hub file both match query; request limit1.
newFindings.observed: Hub search consumes limit with placeholder; proxy then filters placeholder and PC search finds no real match. Final result is empty despite valid hub file.
newFindings.cause: Computer-owned IDs are removed after local search applies its limit.
newFindings.fix: Exclude routed placeholders before matching/limiting local results, then merge genuine backend results under one search policy.
newFindings.test: artifact-api-third-pass.test.ts — redacted locator hits cannot consume limit

newFindings.title: Merged search ignores the requested result limit
newFindings.trigger: One matching hub artifact and one matching computer artifact; public search limit1.
newFindings.observed: Returns two results and scannedCount3 for two artifacts. Each backend received full limit and proxy concatenated results/counts.
newFindings.cause: No final global-per-hub limit/deduplication across local and computer results.
newFindings.fix: Apply one combined limit with correct truncation and distinct artifact accounting. Preserve filtering and stable ordering.
newFindings.test: artifact-api-third-pass.test.ts — one search limit across hub and computer

newFindings.title: Copying a computer file to root puts it in Uploads
newFindings.trigger: Use public artifacts.copy with explicit destFolderId:null, matching UI cut/paste root destination.
newFindings.observed: Hub source copy stays at root; computer source copy lands inside Uploads.
newFindings.cause: Copy invokes chat upload routing, which treats explicit null destination as default-folder request.
newFindings.fix: Distinguish explicit root from unspecified upload destination; preserve requested placement for all storage backends.
newFindings.test: artifact-api-third-pass.test.ts — copy to root preserves explicit destination

newFindings.title: Restored folder membership depends on reconnect order
newFindings.trigger: Public APIs place A-owned file into B-owned folder; restore earlier hub snapshot and reconnect A before B.
newFindings.observed: File is temporarily shown at root with folder_id=null. B-first works. Another forced A recovery after B heals membership. File bytes survive throughout.
newFindings.cause: Recovery provisionally assigns missing parent to A, then A snapshot pruning deletes it and foreign key clears file membership before B arrives.
newFindings.fix: Keep unresolved parent ownership/reference metadata separate from complete authoritative snapshots. Do not prune a provisional cross-computer parent as stale A data.

newFindings.title: Successful history pruning breaks raw file downloads
newFindings.trigger: Prune all saved versions using supported flags while working original still exists.
newFindings.observed: Computer editor/text read succeeds, but REST raw content returns500. Hub control returns200. There was no failed prune or rollback.
newFindings.cause: Computer readBytes resolves a historical version before attempting current working-file read, so history-less current files fail.
newFindings.fix: Serve supported current working originals without requiring a remaining history row. Keep explicit historical version reads validated and do not manufacture versions on reads.
newFindings.test: artifact-api-third-pass.test.ts — pruning all versions preserves raw current read

newFindings.title: Creating a version changes agent attribution to user
newFindings.trigger: Real REST versions POST supplies agent/session author for a computer-owned original.
newFindings.observed: New version has user/null author. Equivalent hub-original request preserves agent attribution.
newFindings.cause: Computer method schema omits author, so parsing strips server-supplied context before shared version creation.
newFindings.fix: Forward and validate author context consistently across hub/computer backends. Preserve real caller attribution; do not guess defaults.
newFindings.test: artifact-api-third-pass.test.ts — REST versions create preserves agent attribution
